title: Murasaki Baby
subtitle: Take a frightened child by the hand
summary: Murasaki Baby is Ovosonico's PlayStation Vita puzzle-platform game, first released in North America on 16 September 2014. The player guides a small girl through a world of children's fears and fantasies by touching her hand and drawing her forward. She carries a heart-shaped balloon, while the unsettling figures and scenery give the journey a deliberately uneasy appearance. The control makes care part of the action. Instead of steering an independent hero with a stick, the player offers a visible point of contact to somebody who may hesitate before following it into the next strange place.
body: Murasaki Baby is Ovosonico's PlayStation Vita puzzle-platform game, first released in North America on 16 September 2014. The player guides a small girl through a world of children's fears and fantasies by touching her hand and drawing her forward. She carries a heart-shaped balloon, while the unsettling figures and scenery give the journey a deliberately uneasy appearance. The control makes care part of the action. Instead of steering an independent hero with a stick, the player offers a visible point of contact to somebody who may hesitate before following it into the next strange place.

Touching other characters' balloons unlocks backdrops with different powers. Swiping the rear touchpad changes the active background, allowing the player to alter the conditions around Baby while continuing to guide her. Puzzles can require quick movement between those powers, connecting the front and back surfaces of the Vita in the same task. The player therefore handles both the child's immediate progress and the environment that makes it possible. A change in scenery is not merely decorative, because it can transform the practical meaning of an obstacle standing in front of her.

Massimo Guarini directed and designed the game after working on Shadows of the Damned. Ovosonico's visual approach draws on illustrated Gothic traditions, giving the child's upside-down face and surrounding creatures a coherent unsettling style. Gianni Ricciardi and Akira Yamaoka contributed music. European and Japanese releases followed shortly after North America. Murasaki Baby gives the Vita's touch controls a narrative purpose: holding a hand and changing the world around it feel like related acts of guidance, allowing the hardware to support the player's relationship with the character rather than simply provide alternative buttons.
